title: The degree of a finite fibre is unchanged by base change (Stacks 03J5 proof, 03J7)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:T\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $X_T=X\times_ST$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projection $f_T:X_T\to T$, let $t\in T$ and $s=g(t)$, with residue fields $\kappa(s)$, $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Suppose that the fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is finite over $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of degree $d=\dim_{\kappa(s)}\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$ (degree as in [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]). Then the fibre $(X_T)_t=X_T\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ of $f_T$ at $t$ is finite over $\kappa(t)$ and $\dim_{\kappa(t)}\Gamma((X_T)_t,\mathcal O_{(X_T)_t})=d$. In particular, if an integer $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound], then $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f_T$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15339 ('X_k = Spec(k) x_{Spec kappa(y)} X_y', and for X_y = Spec(B) the base change is Spec(B tensor k) with dim_k = dim_{kappa(y)} B), and Lemma Tag 03J7 (lemma-base-change-universally-bounded), line 15422

proof.text: *The fibre of $f_T$ is a base change of the fibre of $f$.* Let $g':X_T\to X$ be the first projection, $r:\kappa(s)\to\kappa(t)$ the map induced by $g$ on residue fields, $\pi:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $\pi':(X_T)_t\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ the structure morphisms of the fibres. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] (applied to $f$, $g$, $S'=T$, $s'=t$) there is a morphism $h:(X_T)_t\to X_s$ with $\pi\circ h=\operatorname{Spec}(r)\circ\pi'$ such that $((X_T)_t,h,\pi')$ is a fibre product $X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ of $\pi$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(r)$. (This is the identity $X_k=\operatorname{Spec}(k)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)}X_y$ of the source, for $k=\kappa(t)$.)

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15339

proof.text: *The fibre $X_s$ is $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $\dim_{\kappa(s)}B=d$.* By hypothesis $\pi$ is finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim] (with $k=\kappa(s)$, $T=X_s$, $t=\pi$), $B=\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal O_{X_s})$, a $\kappa(s)$-algebra through $\alpha:\kappa(s)=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s),\mathcal O)\to B$ induced by $\pi$, is finite-dimensional over $\kappa(s)$, and the canonical morphism $\phi:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$: $\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)\circ\phi=\pi$. By the definition of the degree [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound], $d=\dim_{\kappa(s)}B$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15339

proof.text: *Replacing $X_s$ by $\operatorname{Spec}B$.* The triple $((X_T)_t,\phi\circ h,\pi')$ is a fibre product of $\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha):\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(r)$ [def-pc-fibre-product]: it commutes, since $\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)\circ\phi\circ h=\pi\circ h=\operatorname{Spec}(r)\circ\pi'$ (steps 1, 2); and given a scheme $W$ with $a:W\to\operatorname{Spec}B$, $b:W\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)\circ a=\operatorname{Spec}(r)\circ b$, the pair $(\phi^{-1}\circ a,b)$ satisfies $\pi\circ\phi^{-1}\circ a=\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)\circ a=\operatorname{Spec}(r)\circ b$, so by step 1 there is exactly one $w:W\to(X_T)_t$ with $h\circ w=\phi^{-1}\circ a$ and $\pi'\circ w=b$, i.e. exactly one with $\phi\circ h\circ w=a$ and $\pi'\circ w=b$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15339

proof.text: *The fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(t))$ over $\kappa(t)$.* Let $C=B\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(t)$, the tensor product over $\kappa(s)$ for the structure maps $\alpha$ and $r$, and $\psi:\kappa(t)\to C$, $\mu\mapsto1\otimes\mu$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] (with $R=\kappa(s)$, $A=B$, and $\kappa(t)$ in place of its $B$), $\operatorname{Spec}C$ with the projections $\operatorname{Spec}(b\mapsto b\otimes1)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)$ is a fibre product of $\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(r)$. By step 3 and the uniqueness of fibre products up to a unique isomorphism compatible with the projections [def-pc-fibre-product], there is an isomorphism of schemes $\theta:(X_T)_t\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)\circ\theta=\pi'$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15339

proof.text: *$\dim_{\kappa(t)}C=d$.* The field homomorphism $r$ makes $\kappa(t)$ an extension field of $\kappa(s)$, and $C=B\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(t)$ with the $\kappa(t)$-module structure through $\psi$ ($\lambda\cdot(b\otimes\mu)=(1\otimes\lambda)(b\otimes\mu)=b\otimes\lambda\mu$) is the extension of scalars of the $\kappa(s)$-vector space $B$ to $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]. If $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ is a $\kappa(s)$-basis of $B$ (step 2), then $b_1\otimes1,\ldots,b_d\otimes1$ is a $\kappa(t)$-basis of $C$ by that node; so $\dim_{\kappa(t)}C=d$, and in particular $C$ is a finitely generated $\kappa(t)$-module through $\psi$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], i.e. $\psi$ is finite.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15339

proof.text: *$(X_T)_t$ is finite over $\kappa(t)$.* By step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-ring-map-finite], $\operatorname{Spec}(\psi):\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; the isomorphism $\theta$ is finite [lem-weil-pbc-isomorphism-finite]; so $\pi'=\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)\circ\theta$ (step 4) is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. Thus $(X_T)_t$ is finite over $\kappa(t)$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound].

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15339

proof.text: *The degree of $(X_T)_t$ is $d$.* The degree of $(X_T)_t$ over $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound] is the dimension of $\Gamma((X_T)_t,\mathcal O)$ as a $\kappa(t)$-vector space through $\pi'^\sharp\circ\varepsilon_{\kappa(t)}$, where $\varepsilon_R:R\to\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)$ is the canonical isomorphism and $u^\sharp$ the map induced by a morphism $u$ on global sections. Since $\pi'=\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)\circ\theta$, $\pi'^\sharp=\theta^\sharp\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)^\sharp$, and $\theta^\sharp:\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}C,\mathcal O)\to\Gamma((X_T)_t,\mathcal O)$ is a ring isomorphism ($\theta$ is an isomorphism, and taking global sections is functorial). By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-global-sections], $\operatorname{Spec}(\psi)^\sharp\circ\varepsilon_{\kappa(t)}=\varepsilon_C\circ\psi$. Hence the ring isomorphism $\theta^\sharp\circ\varepsilon_C:C\to\Gamma((X_T)_t,\mathcal O)$ satisfies $(\theta^\sharp\circ\varepsilon_C)\circ\psi=\pi'^\sharp\circ\varepsilon_{\kappa(t)}$, so it is $\kappa(t)$-linear, and $\dim_{\kappa(t)}\Gamma((X_T)_t,\mathcal O)=\dim_{\kappa(t)}C=d$ by step 5. (Source: 'for $X_y=\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ the base change is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes k)$ with $\dim_k=\dim_{\kappa(y)}B$'.)

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15339

proof.text: *The bound is preserved.* Suppose $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]. Let $t\in T$ and $s=g(t)$. Then $X_s$ is finite over $\kappa(s)$ of degree $d\le n$, so by steps 6 and 7 $(X_T)_t$ is finite over $\kappa(t)$ of degree $d\le n$. As $t$ was arbitrary, $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f_T$. This is Lemma 03J7, whose proof the source gives as 'clear from Lemma 03J5'.
